symptom: Terminal closure returned MIGRATION_LEDGER_IDENTITY_MISMATCH after the exact migration SQL was applied in production under a Supabase-assigned timestamp that differed from the Git filename timestamp.
root_cause: The terminal migration verifier required byte-identical version+name identity even when the controlled production migration had the same unique stable name and identical intended schema effect but received a new provider timestamp during direct application.
fix: Migration readback v2 keeps exact version+name as first authority and permits reconciliation only when exactly one applied migration has the same stable name. Duplicate same-name candidates remain fail-closed as AMBIGUOUS_NAME.
prevention: Never mark an expected migration green from name alone when multiple applied migrations share that name.
Preserve expected_version and applied_version in readback evidence.
Treat provider-assigned timestamp drift as identity reconciliation, not as missing production application, only when unique-name evidence is unambiguous.
Terminal user handoff remains blocked until migration/provider readback, learning, skill and dashboard writeback are complete.
